# Troubleshooting

## The client cannot connect

<!-- @sdk-kit:keep connect — service-owned: endpoint checks; kept by "sdk-kit sync" -->

- `health()` returns `healthy: false, status: "unreachable"`: the endpoint cannot be reached. Without
  `url` the AWS SDK calls `https://logs.<region>.amazonaws.com`: check the region
  (`GROW_AWS_CLOUDWATCH_LOGS_REGION`, `AWS_REGION`), outbound HTTPS and, behind a proxy, `proxy`.
  With an endpoint override (`GROW_AWS_CLOUDWATCH_LOGS_URL`, `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_CLOUDWATCH_LOGS`,
  `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`, for example Moto on `http://127.0.0.1:5000` or a VPC endpoint) check that it is
  reachable from where your code runs (inside Docker, `127.0.0.1` is the container itself).
- `CONFIG` naming the region: no region was found; set one in code, in the environment or in the AWS
  profile.

<!-- @sdk-kit:endkeep -->

- Calls fail with `UNAVAILABLE` after several seconds: the client retried with backoff. Lower
  `maxRetries` or `totalTimeout` to fail faster.
- Behind a corporate proxy: `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` are **ignored** on purpose. Set `proxy`
  (or `GROW_AWS_CLOUDWATCH_LOGS_PROXY`).

## `CONFIG` errors

The message names the setting or environment variable, never its value. Typical causes: a URL
without `http://` or `https://`, a duration such as `10 sec` (use `10s` or `10000`), a client
certificate without its key, `MAX_RETRIES` below 0.

## `AUTHENTICATION` or `PERMISSION_DENIED`

- `ping()` is the quickest credential check: it makes one authenticated call.

<!-- @sdk-kit:keep authentication — service-owned: which credentials the SDK reads; kept by "sdk-kit sync" -->

- Credentials come from the AWS default chain (environment, shared config and SSO, web identity,
  container and instance roles) unless `accessKeyId`/`secretAccessKey`, `profile`, `credentials` or
  `roleArn` is set; explicit config values win over the environment. When
  `GROW_AWS_CLOUDWATCH_LOGS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` is set, the secret key and session token are read from
  `GROW_AWS_CLOUDWATCH_LOGS_*` only, never mixed with `AWS_*` (see
  [Service settings](functions.md#service-configuration)).
- `AUTHENTICATION`: the key is unknown, expired (temporary credentials need `sessionToken`) or the
  clock is skewed. `PERMISSION_DENIED`: the IAM policy lacks the `logs:` permission for the
  operation named in the message; with `roleArn` the caller also needs `sts:AssumeRole`.

<!-- @sdk-kit:endkeep -->

- The SDK never prints credentials, so `toString()` of the config shows `[REDACTED]` even when a
  credential is set.

## TLS errors

- Self-signed or private CA: set `tls.caCertPath` (`GROW_AWS_CLOUDWATCH_LOGS_CA_CERT`).
- Mutual TLS: set both `tls.clientCertPath` and `tls.clientKeyPath`.
- `tls.insecureSkipVerify` only for local tests.

## `RATE_LIMITED`

The service asked the client to slow down. The client waits for `Retry-After` up to
`maxRetryAfter` (60 s); longer waits fail at once with `retryAfter` set on the error so your code
can schedule a later attempt.

## `TIMEOUT`

`requestTimeout` (30 s) bounds one attempt and `totalTimeout` (120 s) the whole call including
retries. Raise them for slow operations, or pass a per-call deadline (signal, ctx, cancel token,
future timeout).

## See what the client does

Turn on the [logger](hooks.md#logger) or add [hooks](hooks.md#hooks): both see every attempt with
redacted headers and URLs.

## Docker integration tests fail

- Run one language: `make test-docker LANGS=go`.
- In CI, download the `compose-logs-<lang>` artifact of the failed job.
- Locally, the stack is removed after each run; rerun with Docker logs open
  (`docker compose -f docker/compose.yml logs -f`) in a second terminal.

<!-- @sdk-kit:keep service — service-owned: Amazon CloudWatch Logs-specific problems (own ## sections); kept by "sdk-kit sync" -->

## `putLogEvents` reports rejected events or more batches than expected

- One `PutLogEvents` call may not span more than 24 hours, so the SDK splits the timestamp-sorted
  events into several batches. Events older than 14 days (or older than the group's retention) are
  usually more than 24 hours older than the rest, so they end up in **their own batch**, which AWS
  rejects as a whole: `batches` is higher and `rejected` counts them, with `rejectedInfo`
  (`tooOldLogEventEndIndex`, `expiredLogEventEndIndex`) pointing into that batch. Events more than
  2 hours in the future are rejected as too new. Rejected events are never retried.
- See [Ingest](functions/ingest.md) for the limits and the index semantics.

## Error messages do not show the AWS error text

On purpose: AWS error messages can echo request data (log messages, group names, filter patterns),
so the SDK never copies them. The message is `"<operation>: <reason>[: <AwsCode>] (HTTP <status>)"`
(the AWS error code for every code in the [error mapping](compatibility.md#error-mapping)), and the
error carries the AWS request id, which is what AWS Support needs. The original AWS SDK error stays
available as the redacted cause.

<!-- @sdk-kit:endkeep -->
